Hello, I want to ask about recipes. I am living alone in a studio in Drumul Taberei, small kitchen with only two plates for cooking, so please give me simple ones.
I work as receptionist in a dental clinic in Sector 6, the program is 8 to 4.
For going to work I take the 41 tram, it is about 25 minutes, sometimes more in winter.
Can you help me with English for job interviews? My level is B1.
I have an online English teacher, the lesson is every Tuesday evening.
I have a old Samsung Galaxy A12, the storage is always full with photos.
I have a cat, Pufi, she is grey and very lazy.
My sister Ioana lives in Cluj and she is pregnant, the baby comes in July.

Please, what is good gift for a nurse? Oh, I must tell you, from Monday I am not more at the dental clinic, I start as administrative assistant at Floreasca hospital, and it is far so I will take metro instead of the 41.
The program at the hospital is in shifts, some weeks morning and some weeks afternoon.
Now I go with metro M1 to the hospital, around 30 minutes, very crowded in the morning.
I want to make a cake for Ioana, she is now 7 months. Do you have a recipe without oven? In my studio I have only the two plates.
My English teacher moved the lesson to Thursday evening, it is more good for my shifts.
Finally I bought new phone, iPhone 13 second hand from OLX, now I have space for all Pufi photos.
My friend Andreea also works at Floreasca now, in the laboratory.
Next week I go to Constanta for three days at the sea with my colleagues.
Big news! I moved from the studio, now I rent a two rooms apartment in Titan with a real kitchen with oven!
Ioana had the baby, a boy named Matei, everybody is healthy.
From Titan I take the 311 bus to the hospital, the metro is not good from here.
Can you suggest name for a second cat? I adopted a small black kitten, Pufi is jealous.
My level in English now is B2, I passed the test!
I still work at Floreasca hospital, now I know everybody there.
I was thinking maybe to go work in Germany one day, but not now.
The kitchen in Titan has an oven so finally I made the cake I wanted, for Matei's party.
From this month the hospital moved me to fixed morning program, no more afternoon shifts.

I am a retired teacher of mathematics.
I live in Stuttgart-Degerloch, in the house where I raised my children.
Klaus and I have been married for forty-four years.
My husband Klaus and I walk in the Schönbuch forest every Sunday.
I take Ramipril 5 mg for my blood pressure every morning.
We drive a Mercedes B-Klasse, which Klaus maintains meticulously.
I sing in the choir of the Michaelskirche on Thursday evenings.
Our daughter Sabine lives in Hamburg with her two children.
I read the Stuttgarter Zeitung every morning, the paper edition.
The physician has increased the Ramipril to 10 mg.
The keys to the flat in Vaihingen were handed over to us on Friday; the house has been sold.
The flat in Vaihingen has a lift, which is a relief for Klaus's knees.
Sabine has accepted a position in Munich and intends to move there in the autumn.
Klaus passed away peacefully on the third of June.
I have sold the car; the Stadtbahn stops directly in front of the building.
I now walk in the Schönbuch on Sundays with my neighbour, Frau Albrecht.
The choir of the Michaelskirche remains my great joy on Thursdays.
My former colleague Herr Brandt has begun teaching again at seventy.
My subscription is now the digital edition of the Stuttgarter Zeitung; the paper was simply too much.
On Saturday I shall attend a choir festival in Esslingen, for one day only.
Sabine and the children have settled in Munich.
Since the move I sing in the choir of the Vaihingen Stadtkirche instead; the Michaelskirche was too far.
I have begun to learn Italian at the Volkshochschule on Tuesday mornings.
I am considering a trip to Rome next spring to practise my Italian.
In addition to Italian I have taken up watercolour painting.
The physician has replaced the Ramipril with Candesartan because of the cough.
Hi! I'm a backend developer at a logistics startup here in Santiago, mostly working with Go and Postgres. Could you explain how connection pooling works in pgx? I'd love a deep dive.
Some context: I live in Ñuñoa with my girlfriend Camila.
Camila and I have been together for five years now.
We have a very energetic border collie named Tango.
There's a dog park two blocks from our place in Ñuñoa where Tango runs every evening.
I usually commute by metro, line 3 to Providencia, about 25 minutes each way, which gives me time to read.
I've been doing intermittent fasting, 16:8, for about three months, and I'm curious how it interacts with endurance training.
I run with a club on Saturday mornings in Parque Bicentenario, usually around 15 km.
My laptop is a 2019 MacBook Pro with an Intel chip, and Docker builds take forever on it.
Could you help me prepare for system design interviews? Quick update: I accepted an offer from a fintech in Las Condes and start in March, so my Go work at the logistics company is wrapping up.
The fintech handed me an M3 MacBook Air and honestly Docker builds feel instant now. Can you suggest a good dotfiles setup for a fresh machine?
Since the new office is in Las Condes, I've switched to biking along the Andrés Bello path. It's around 40 minutes but way more pleasant than line 3.
I'm still doing 16:8 fasting, though I sometimes shift the window on long-run days.
Camila just started a master's in urban planning at the Universidad Católica and I'm so proud of her!
We're spending Semana Santa in Valparaíso, just four days by the sea.
Tango has a new friend: we adopted a rescue kitten named Pisco, and they get along surprisingly well.
Can you help me plan a marathon build? Also, I left the Saturday club; I train alone with a plan now because their pace didn't fit marathon prep.
Big change at home: Camila and I moved to a bigger apartment in Providencia with a balcony, partly so Tango has more space.
From Providencia the bike ride to the Las Condes office is only 20 minutes now.
I've stopped intermittent fasting completely; my dietitian thought it was hurting my recovery during the marathon block.
My brother Diego bought an M3 MacBook Air too after trying mine.
I keep thinking about moving to Lisbon someday for the tech scene, but it's just a daydream for now.
Still on the Go team at the fintech, and now I'm also mentoring two juniors, which I enjoy.
Ran the Santiago marathon in 3:41, my first one ever!
Camila and I got engaged on our trip to the south!
I'm switching teams at the fintech to the payments platform group, so it's mostly Rust now instead of Go.
